svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The anthers split open and release pollen grains, each carrying male gametes."], [3, "Pollination: an insect carries a pollen grain from the anther of another flower of the same species to this stigma (cross-pollination). The sticky stigma holds it."], [6, "A pollen tube grows out of the grain, down through the style and into the ovary, and enters an ovule through the micropyle. The male gamete nucleus travels down the tube."], [10, "Fertilisation: the male gamete nucleus fuses with the female gamete (egg cell) nucleus in the ovule, forming a zygote that will grow into the embryo."], [13, "After fertilisation the ovule develops into a seed and the ovary into a fruit. The petals, sepals and stamens wither and fall off."]]
svg.title: Half-flower of an insect-pollinated flower
svg.desc: Longitudinal section of an insect-pollinated flower showing the flower stalk, receptacle, sepals, petals with nectaries, stamens (anther and filament) and the carpel (stigma, style and ovary with ovules).
svg.text: Half-flower: longitudinal section of an insect-pollinated flower
Cut through the middle: the parts in the cut plane are shown. Simplified; not to scale.

g.data-info: Supports the flower and holds it where pollinators can reach it.
Green, leaf-like structures that protected the flower when it was a bud.
The top of the flower stalk, to which all the other flower parts are attached.
Brightly coloured and often scented, to attract insect pollinators.
Makes nectar, a sugary liquid that rewards insects; reaching it, they brush against anthers and stigma.
Part of the stamen: the stalk that holds the anther up in a position where insects brush against it.
Part of the stamen: contains pollen sacs in which pollen grains (holding the male gametes) are made by meiosis. It splits open to release pollen.
Part of the carpel: the swollen base containing the ovules. After fertilisation it develops into the fruit.
Contains a female gamete (egg cell). The pollen tube enters through a small gap, the micropyle. After fertilisation the ovule becomes a seed.
Part of the carpel: holds up the stigma. After pollination a pollen tube grows down through it to the ovary.
Part of the carpel: a sticky surface at the top that catches pollen grains during pollination.

g.text: 2 Pollination: pollen lands on the stigma
3 A pollen tube grows to an ovule
4 Fertilisation: male and female gamete nuclei fuse
5 Ovule becomes a seed; ovary becomes a fruit
